content: These references pertain to studies, reviews, and technical advancements in the field of tuberculosis (TB) diagnostics, drug resistance, and treatment methodologies. 1. The 2022 WHO report on tuberculosis provides comprehensive data on the global burden of TB, including updates on diagnostics, treatment, and drug resistance trends. It was accessed on March 21, 2023. 2. Mohamed S, Köser CU, Salfinger M, et al. discuss the potential of targeted next-generation sequencing as a versatile tool for mycobacterial diagnostics in their 2021 study published in the European Respiratory Journal. 3. The 2013 Global Tuberculosis Report by the WHO outlines the epidemiology, challenges, and progress in TB control efforts worldwide. It was accessed on June 18, 2023. 4. A technical report by the WHO details critical concentrations for drug susceptibility testing of isoniazid and rifamycins, including rifampicin, rifabutin, and rifapentine. This report was accessed on August 13, 2021. 5. The WHO's 2021 consolidated guidelines on TB diagnosis emphasize the use of rapid diagnostic tools for TB detection, providing updated recommendations for clinical practice. 6. Miotto P, Tessema B, Tagliani E, et al. propose a standardized method for interpreting the relationship between genetic mutations and phenotypic drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis in their 2017 publication in the European Respiratory Journal. 7. Köser CU, Maurer FP, and Kranzer K highlight the importance of drug susceptibility testing for bedaquiline and delamanid to prevent repeating past errors in TB treatment strategies. 8. Alagna R, Cabibbe AM, Miotto P, et al. evaluate the practical application of the new WHO definition of extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis in their 2021 study. 9. Ness T, Van LH, Petermane I, et al. emphasize the risks of introducing new anti-TB drugs without adequate diagnostic capacity, as discussed in their 2023 publication in Breathe. 10. The WHO's July 2023 rapid communication highlights the use of targeted next-generation sequencing to detect drug-resistant TB, underscoring its potential for improving diagnostic accuracy. 11. Nebenzahl-Guimaraes H, Jacobson KR, Farhat MR, et al. systematically review allelic exchange experiments to identify mutations conferring drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. 12. Walker TM, Kohl TA, Omar SV, et al. demonstrate the utility of whole-genome sequencing for predicting drug susceptibility and resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis in a retrospective cohort study published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 13. Kadura S, King N, Nakhoul M, et al. systematically review mutations associated with resistance to new and repurposed TB drugs, including bedaquiline, clofazimine, linezolid, delamanid, and pretomanid. 14. The WHO's second edition of the mutation catalog for Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex provides a detailed association between genetic mutations and drug resistance, aiding in diagnostic and treatment decisions. 15. A technical report by the WHO outlines optimized broth microdilution plate methodologies for drug susceptibility testing of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex. 16. Bateson A, Ortiz Canseco J, McHugh TD, et al. investigate differences in intrinsic susceptibility of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex to pretomanid, revealing ancient and recent variations. 17. The WHO's breakpoint tables for interpreting minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) and zone diameters provide critical guidance for TB drug susceptibility testing. 18. Line probe assays for detecting drug-resistant TB are detailed in a WHO manual, offering interpretation and reporting guidelines for laboratory staff and clinicians. 19. Gomes LC, Campino S, Marinho CRF, et al. use whole-genome sequencing to identify large deletions and loss-of-function mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis drug resistance genes. 20. The Antimycobacterial Susceptibility Testing Group discusses updated approaches to defining susceptibility and resistance to anti-TB agents, with implications for diagnosis and treatment. 21. The CRyPTIC Consortium establishes epidemiological cut-off values for high-throughput antibiotic susceptibility testing of Mycobacterium tuberculosis using a 96-well broth microdilution plate. 22. Köser CU, Maurer FP emphasize the need for detailed analysis of MICs and sequencing data to establish provisional epidemiological cut-off values for Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex. 23. Kahlmeter G, Turnidge J advocate for a systematic approach to determining epidemiological cut-off values based on quality-controlled MIC series. 24. The CRyPTIC Consortium responds to discussions on epidemiological cut-off values for high-throughput antibiotic susceptibility testing of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. 25. Hall MB, Coin LJM assess the 2021 WHO Mycobacterium tuberculosis drug resistance mutation catalog using an independent dataset. 26. Ajileye A, Alvarez N, Merker M, et al. identify systematic false-positive fluoroquinolone resistance results caused by certain gyrA mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. 27. Beckert P, Sanchez-Padilla E, Merker M, et al. report on a multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis outbreak clone in Eswatini with elevated bedaquiline resistance predating treatment. 28. Köser CU, Robledo J, Shubladze N, et al. call for guidance to mitigate the consequences of analytical errors during antimicrobial susceptibility testing for TB. 29. The WHO standard for universal access to rapid TB diagnostics emphasizes the importance of timely and accurate diagnostic tools for TB control. 30. André E, Goeminne L, Cabibbe AM, et al. propose a consensus numbering system for rifampicin resistance-associated rpoB gene mutations in pathogenic mycobacteria. 31. Köser CU, Georghiou SB, Schön T, et al. discuss the consequences of poorly defined breakpoints for rifampin susceptibility testing of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex. 32. The use of next-generation sequencing technologies for detecting mutations associated with drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex is detailed in a WHO technical guide. 33. The RealTime MTB RIF/INH Resistance Amplification Reagent Kit provides instructions for detecting rifampicin and isoniazid resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. 34. The BD MAX™ MDR-TB assay offers a molecular diagnostic tool for detecting multidrug-resistant TB. 35. The Xpert® MTB/RIF Ultra assay provides enhanced sensitivity for detecting Mycobacterium tuberculosis and rifampicin resistance. 36. The Truenat® MTB-RIF Dx assay offers a rapid molecular diagnostic solution for detecting rifampicin resistance in TB. 37. The GenoScholar™ PZA-TB II assay detects pncA mutations associated with pyrazinamide resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. 38. The Cobas® MTB-RIF/INH assay provides molecular diagnostics for rifampicin and isoniazid resistance in TB. 39. Anthony RM, Tagliani E, Nikolaevskyy V, et al. share experiences from four years of organizing external quality assessments for Mycobacterium tuberculosis whole-genome sequencing in the EU/EEA. 40. Ando H, Miyoshi-Akiyama T, Watanabe S, et al. identify a silent mutation in mabA that confers isoniazid resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. 41. Vilchèze C, Wang F, Arai M, et al. demonstrate that transferring a point mutation in Mycobacterium tuberculosis inhA resolves the target of isoniazid. 42. Machado D, Perdigão J, Ramos J, et al. associate high-level resistance to isoniazid and ethionamide in multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis of the Lisboa family with inhA double mutations. 43. Ghodousi A, Tagliani E, Karunaratne E, et al. describe isoniazid resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis as a heterogeneous phenotype with overlapping MIC distributions and different resistance mechanisms. 44. Napier G, Campino S, Phelan JE, et al. conduct large-scale genomic analysis of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, revealing the extent of target and compensatory mutations linked to multidrug-resistant TB. 45. Safi H, Lingaraju S, Amin A, et al. explore the evolution of high-level ethambutol-resistant TB through interacting mutations in decaprenyl phosphoryl-ß-D-arabinose biosynthetic and utilization pathway genes. 46. Gygli SM, Keller PM, Ballif M, et al. use whole-genome sequencing to predict drug resistance profiles in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. 47. Nonghanphithak D, Kaewprasert O, Chaiyachat P, et al. analyze whole-genome sequences to compare drug-resistance mutations and MICs in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates causing MDR/XDR-TB. 48. Loiseau C, Menardo F, Aseffa A, et al. trace the African origin of Mycobacterium bovis in their study published in Evolutionary Medicine and Public Health. 49. Tagliani E, Hassan MO, Waberi Y, et al. reveal high levels of drug-resistant TB in Djibouti through culture and next-generation sequencing-based drug susceptibility testing. 50. Briquet A, Vong R, Roseau JB, et al. describe the clinical features of Mycobacterium canettii infection in a retrospective study of 20 cases among French soldiers and their relatives. 51. Feuerriegel S, Köser CU, Richter E, et al. report that Mycobacterium canettii is intrinsically resistant to both pyrazinamide and pyrazinoic acid. 52. Willby MJ, Wijkander M, Havumaki J, et al. compare the detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis pncA mutations by the Nipro GenoScholar PZA-TB II assay to conventional sequencing. 53. Köser CU, Cirillo DM, Miotto P discuss the optimal combination of genotypic and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing methods for pyrazinamide. 54. Köser CU, Ellington MJ, Peacock SJ highlight the role of whole-genome sequencing in controlling antimicrobial resistance. 55. Brankin AE, Fowler PW demonstrate that including minor alleles improves catalog-based prediction of fluoroquinolone resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. 56. Huitric E, Verhasselt P, Koul A, et al. investigate the rates and mechanisms of resistance development in Mycobacterium tuberculosis to a novel diarylquinoline ATP synthase inhibitor. 57. Andries K, Villellas C, Coeck N, et al. describe acquired resistance of Mycobacterium tuberculosis to bedaquiline in their study published in PLoS One. 58. Hartkoorn RC, Upekar S, Cole ST report cross-resistance between clofazimine and bedaquiline due to up-regulation of MmpL5 in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. 59. Almeida D, Ioerger T, Tyagi S, et al. identify mutations in pepQ that confer low-level resistance to bedaquiline and clofazimine in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. 60. Sarathy J, Blanc L, Alvarez-Cabrera N, et al. demonstrate that fluoroquinolone efficacy against TB is driven by penetration into lesions and activity at the site of infection.
